questions.text: What does the following C-statement declare?
questions.optA: A function that takes an integer pointer as argument and returns an integer
questions.optB: A function that takes an integer as argument and returns an integer pointer
questions.optC: A pointer to a function that takes an integer pointer as argument and returns an integer.
questions.optD: A function that takes an integer pointer as argument and returns a function pointer
questions.subject: 8. C Prog

questions.optB: A data type that cannot be instantiated
questions.optC: A data type for which only the operations defined on it can be used, but none else
questions.subject: 8. C Prog
questions.referenceAnswer: An abstract data type is specified through its permitted operations and their behavior. Its representation is hidden from clients. An abstract class and a noninstantiable type are different concepts.

questions.text: A common property of logic programming languages and functional languages is:
questions.subject: 8. C Prog
questions.referenceAnswer: Both paradigms describe the required relations or results declaratively. Logic programming commonly uses Horn clauses; functional programming is associated with lambda calculus. Those foundations are not shared by both paradigms.

questions.text:
Which one of the following are essential features of an object-oriented programming language?
(i) Abstraction and encapsulation
(ii) Strictly-typedness
(iii) Type-safe property coupled with sub-type rule
(iv) Polymorphism in the presence of inheritance
questions.subject: 8. C Prog
questions.referenceAnswer: The conventional language-paradigm answer is abstraction/encapsulation and inheritance-based polymorphism. Dynamic object-oriented languages show that strict static typing and the stated subtype safety property are not essential to the paradigm.

questions.text:
An undirected graph $G$ has $n$ nodes. Its adjacency matrix is given by an $n\times n$ square matrix whose
1. diagonal elements are 0's, and
2. non-diagonal elements are 1's.
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.optA: Graph G has no minimum spanning tree (MST)
questions.optB: Graph $G$ has a unique MST of cost $n-1$
questions.optC: Graph $G$ has multiple distinct MST's, each of cost $n-1$
questions.optD: Graph G has multiple spanning trees of different costs
questions.subject: 7. Algorithms
questions.referenceAnswer: The adjacency matrix describes the unit-weight complete graph. Every spanning tree uses n-1 unit edges and is minimum. For n at least 3 there are multiple trees. The unstated small cases n=1 or n=2 are exceptions to multiplicity; C is the intended general-case answer.

questions.text: Let $A, B$ and $C$ be non-empty sets and let $X = (A - B) - C$ and $Y = (A - C) - (B - C)$ Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Both expressions contain exactly the elements of A that are in neither B nor C. Algebraically each equals A intersect complement(B) intersect complement(C). Hence X=Y.

questions.text: The following is the Hasse diagram of the poset $[\{a, b, c, d, e\}, \leq]$ [IMG_1] The poset is
questions.optB: a lattice but not a distributive lattice
questions.optC: a distributive lattice but not a Boolean algebra
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: The diagram is the five-element diamond lattice M3. Meets and joins exist, but distributivity fails: b meet (c join d)=b, whereas (b meet c) join (b meet d)=e. It is not a Boolean algebra.

questions.text: Let $G$ be a simple connected planar graph with 13 vertices and 19 edges. Then, the number of faces in the planar embedding of the graph is
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Euler's formula for a connected planar embedding is V-E+F=2. Therefore F=2-13+19=8, including the unbounded face.

questions.text: Let $G$ be a simple graph with 20 vertices and 100 edges. The size of the minimum vertex cover of $G$ is 8. Then, the size of the maximum independent set of $G$ is
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: The complement of a vertex cover is an independent set, and conversely. Thus the maximum independent set has 20-8=12 vertices.

questions.text: Let $f(x)$ be the continuous probability density function of a random variable $X$. The probability that $a<X\le b$, is
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Probability over an interval is the integral of the density on that interval. Since the distribution is continuous, endpoint inclusion makes no difference: integrate f(x) from a to b.

questions.text: Normally user programs are prevented from handling I/O directly by I/O instructions in them. For CPUs having explicit I/O instructions, such I/O protection is ensured by having the I/O instructions privileged. In a CPU with memory mapped I/O, there is no explicit I/O instruction. Which one of the following is true for a CPU with memory mapped I/O?

questions.optB: I/O protection is ensured by a hardware trap

questions.text: The maximum window size for data transmission using the selective reject protocol with $n$-bit frame sequence numbers is:
questions.subject: 3. Computer Networks
questions.referenceAnswer: Selective repeat/reject must reserve half the sequence-number space to distinguish new frames from delayed duplicates. With n-bit sequence numbers the maximum window is 2^(n-1).

questions.text: In a network of LANs connected by bridges, packets are sent from one LAN to another through intermediate bridges. Since more than one path may exist between two LANs, packets may have to be routed through multiple bridges. Why is the spanning tree algorithm used for bridge routing?
questions.optA: For shortest path routing between LANs
questions.optB: For avoiding loops in the routing paths
questions.subject: 3. Computer Networks
questions.referenceAnswer: Bridges flood some frames, which can circulate indefinitely in a cyclic topology. A spanning tree removes forwarding loops while retaining connectivity; it need not minimize every source-destination route.

10, 8, 5, 3, 2

questions.text: Let $P$, $Q$ and $R$ be three atomic propositional assertions. Let $X$ denote $(P \vee Q) \rightarrow R$ and $Y$ denote $(P \rightarrow R) \vee (Q \rightarrow R)$. Which one of the following is a tautology?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: X requires R whenever either P or Q holds. Y requires only one of the two implications. If X is true then Y is true; P=true,Q=false,R=false makes Y true but X false, disproving equivalence and the reverse implication.

questions.text: What is the first order predicate calculus statement equivalent to the following? Every teacher is liked by some student
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: For each object x that is a teacher, there must exist an object y such that y is a student AND y likes x. The existential witness may differ for different teachers. Only B expresses that scope and conjunction.

questions.text: Let $R$ and $S$ be any two equivalence relations on a non-empty set $A$. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.optA: $R\cup S$, $R\cap S$ are both equivalence relations
questions.optD: Neither $R \cup S$ nor $R \cap S$ is an equivalence relation
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: An intersection retains reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. A union need not be transitive: one relation can supply (a,b), another (b,c), without either supplying (a,c).

questions.text: Let $f: B \rightarrow C$ and $g: A \rightarrow B$ be two functions and let $h = f \circ g$. Given that $h$ is an onto function. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.optA: f and g should both be onto functions
questions.optB: f should be onto but g need not be onto
questions.optC: g should be onto but f not be onto
questions.optD: both f and g need not be onto
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: For every c in C, surjectivity of f composed with g provides an a with f(g(a))=c, so f is onto. Elements of B outside g(A) need never be visited, so g need not be onto.

questions.text: What is the minimum number of ordered pairs of non-negative numbers that should be chosen to ensure that there are two pairs $(a,b)$ and $(c,d)$ in the chosen set such that $a \equiv c \pmod{3}$ and $b \equiv d \pmod{5}$
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: There are 3 times 5=15 possible residue pairs (a mod 3,b mod 5). Sixteen choices force a repeated residue pair by the pigeonhole principle; fifteen need not. Non-negative numbers are interpreted as integers for modular congruence.

questions.text: Consider three decision problems $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$. It is known that $P_1$ is decidable and $P_2$ is undecidable. Which one of the following is true?
questions.optA: $P_3$ is decidable if $P_1$ is reducible to $P_3$
questions.optB: $P_3$ is undecidable if $P_3$ is reducible to $P_2$
questions.optC: $P_3$ is undecidable if $P_2$ is reducible to $P_3$
questions.optD: $P_3$ is decidable if $P_3$ is reducible to $P_2$'s complement
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: If the known undecidable problem P2 reduces effectively to P3, a decider for P3 would decide P2. Thus P3 must be undecidable. Reducing a decidable problem to P3 gives no such conclusion.

questions.text: Consider the set H of all $3 \times 3$ matrices of the type $$ \begin{bmatrix} a & f & e \\ 0 & b & d \\ 0 & 0 & c \end{bmatrix} $$ where a, b, c, d, e and f are real numbers and $abc \neq 0$. Under the matrix multiplication operation, the set H is
questions.optC: a semigroup but not a monoid
questions.optD: neither a group nor a semigroup
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: These are the invertible upper triangular real matrices: determinant abc is nonzero. Products and inverses remain upper triangular with nonzero diagonal, and the identity belongs to the set. Associativity is inherited from matrix multiplication.

questions.text:

The graphs G1, G2, G3 and G4 appear in source order in options A, B, C and D.

Consider the following system of equations in three real variables $x_1,x_2,x_3$:
$$\begin{aligned}2x_1-x_2-3x_3&=1\\3x_1+2x_2+5x_3&=2\\-x_1+4x_2+x_3&=3\end{aligned}$$
This system of equations has

questions.text:
What are the eigenvalues of the following $2\times2$ matrix?
$$\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-4&5\end{bmatrix}$$
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: The characteristic polynomial is (2-lambda)(5-lambda)-4=lambda^2-7lambda+6=(lambda-1)(lambda-6). The eigenvalues are 1 and 6.

questions.text: Let $G(x) = \frac{1}{(1-x)^2} = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} g(i)x^i$ where $|x| < 1$. What is $g(i)$?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Differentiate the geometric series, or convolve two copies of it. The coefficient of x^i in (1-x)^(-2) is i+1. The selected scan has five choices (including an extra leading 1), so its answer is C; the four-option book and discussion call the same expression B.

issues: Selected scan prints five options A=1,B=i,C=i+1,D=2i,E=2^i. Book/discussion omit A=1 and key i+1 as B. Final source key is C.

questions.text: Box $P$ has 2 red balls and 3 blue balls and box $Q$ has 3 red balls and 1 blue ball. A ball is selected as follows: (i) select a box (ii) choose a ball from the selected box such that each ball in the box is equally likely to be chosen. The probabilities of selecting boxes $P$ and $Q$ are $1/3$ and $2/3$, respectively. Given that a ball selected in the above process is a red ball, the probability that it came from the box $P$ is:
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: P(P and red)=(1/3)(2/5)=2/15. Total red probability is 2/15+(2/3)(3/4)=19/30. Bayes' rule gives (2/15)/(19/30)=4/19.

questions.text: A random bit string of length $n$ is constructed by tossing a fair coin $n$ times and setting a bit to 0 or 1 depending on outcomes head and tail, respectively. The probability that two such randomly generated strings are not identical is:
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Each of the n independent bit positions matches with probability 1/2. Equality has probability 2^(-n); its complement is 1-2^(-n).

questions.text: Consider the machine M: [IMG_1] The language recognized by M is
questions.optA: $\{w \in \{a, b\}^* \mid \text{every } a \text{ in } w \text{ is followed by exactly two } b\text{'s}\}$
questions.optB: $\{w \in \{a, b\}^* \text{ every } a \text{ in } w \text{ is followed by at least two } b\text{'s}\}$
questions.optD: $\{w \in \{a, b\}^* w \text{ does not contain 'aa' as a substring}\}$
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: The states track progress through a,b,b. Once abb has been seen the accepting state loops on both symbols. Therefore acceptance means the input contains abb somewhere; it does not constrain every occurrence of a.

questions.text: Let $N_f$ and $N_p$ denote the classes of languages accepted by non-deterministic finite automata and non-deterministic push-down automata, respectively. Let $D_f$ and $D_p$ denote the classes of languages accepted by deterministic finite automata and deterministic push-down automata, respectively. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: Nondeterminism does not increase finite-automaton language power: Df=Nf is the regular languages. Deterministic context-free languages form a proper subset of the languages accepted by nondeterministic pushdown automata.

questions.text: Consider the languages $L_1=\{a^n b^n c^m : n,m>0\}$ and $L_2=\{a^n b^m c^m + n,m>0\}$. Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.optD: $L_1 \cap L_2$ is a context sensitive language
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: Under the conventional reading of the malformed separator in L2, the languages are {a^n b^n c^m} and {a^n b^m c^m} for positive n,m. Their intersection is {a^n b^n c^n}, which is not context-free. Each component and their union are context-free, while the intersection is context-sensitive. If the extra printed plus is read as literal syntax, L2 is not a standard language specification, so this scan is self-assessed.

issues: The source separator after c^m in L2 is malformed, appearing as + n,m>0 on the next line. Literal expression retained; conventional intended language uses a separator before n,m>0. No automatic grading.

questions.text: Let $L_1$ be a recursive language, and let $L_2$ be a recursively enumerable but not a recursive language. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.optA: $\bar{L_1}$ is recursive and $\bar{L_2}$ is recursively enumerable
questions.optB: $\bar{L_1}$ is recursive and $\bar{L_2}$ is not recursively enumerable
questions.optD: $\bar{L_1}$ is recursively enumerable and $\bar{L_2}$ is recursive
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: Recursive languages are closed under complement, so complement(L1) is recursive. If complement(L2) were recursively enumerable as well as L2, dovetailing their recognizers would decide L2, contradicting the premise.

questions.text:
Consider the languages: 
$L_1 = \{ww^R \mid w \in \{0, 1\}^*\}$ 
$L_2 = \{w \# w^R \mid w \in \{0, 1\}^*\}$, where $\#$ is a special symbol 
$L_3 = \{ww \mid w \in \{0, 1\}^*\}$ 
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.optC: $L_3$ is a CFL, but not a deterministic CFL
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: The special separator marks the midpoint in L2. A deterministic pushdown automaton pushes the first word and pops while checking its reverse after the separator. Unmarked even palindromes require nondeterminism, and unrestricted copying ww is not context-free.

questions.text:
Consider the following two problems on undirected graphs:
$\alpha$: Given $G(V,E)$, does $G$ have an independent set of size $|V|-4$?
$\beta$: Given $G(V,E)$, does $G$ have an independent set of size 5?
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.subject: 7. Algorithms
questions.optA: $\alpha$ is in P and $\beta$ is NP-complete
questions.optB: $\alpha$ is NP-complete and $\beta$ is in P
questions.referenceAnswer: An independent set of |V|-4 exists exactly when a vertex cover of at most 4 exists; enumerate all 4-subsets in polynomial time. A size-5 independent set can similarly be found by enumerating all 5-subsets. Both constants are fixed, hence both problems are in P.

questions.text:
Consider a three word machine instruction
$\mathrm{ADD}\ A[R_0], @B$
The first operand (destination) 'A [R0]' uses indexed addressing mode with R0 as the index register. The second operand (source) "@B" uses indirect addressing mode. A and B are memory addresses residing at the second and the third words, respectively. The first word of the instruction specifies the opcode, the index register designation and the source and destination addressing modes. During execution of ADD instruction, the two operands are added and stored in the destination (first operand).
The number of memory cycles needed during the execution cycle of the instruction is
questions.subject: 4. COA
questions.referenceAnswer: After the opcode fetch, read the two address words A and B; read the destination at A+R0; read the pointer at B; read the source at that pointer; and write the sum to the destination. These are six memory cycles in the execution phase.

questions.text: A device with data transfer rate 10 KB/sec is connected to a CPU. Data is transferred byte-wise. Let the interrupt overhead be $4\ \mu\text{sec}$. The byte transfer time between the device interface register and CPU or memory is negligible. What is the minimum performance gain of operating the device under interrupt mode over operating it under program controlled mode?
questions.subject: 4. COA
questions.referenceAnswer: Using the conventional decimal interpretation of 10 KB/s, each byte arrives every 100 microseconds. Polling occupies that interval; interrupt service costs 4 microseconds, giving a CPU-time ratio of 100/4=25. With binary KiB the ratio is 24.414; the listed 25 uses decimal KB.

questions.subject: 4. COA

questions.text: Suppose n processes, $P_1,\ldots,P_n$, share m identical resource units, which can be reserved and released one at a time. The maximum resource requirement of process $P_i$ is $s_i$, where $s_i>0$. Which one of the following is a sufficient condition for ensuring that deadlock does not occur?
questions.subject: 5. Operating Systems
questions.referenceAnswer: If every process holds at most si-1 resources without finishing, total held is at most sum(si)-n. The condition sum(si)<m+n leaves at least one resource available, enabling some process to finish and release resources. The duplicated source distractors A and B only bound each individual demand and do not prevent deadlock. For example, two processes each needing 3 of 4 resources may each hold 2 and wait forever.

questions.text: In a packet switching network, packets are routed from source to destination along a single path having two intermediate nodes. If the message size is 24 bytes and each packet contains a header of 3 bytes, then the optimum packet size is

Statement for Linked Answer Questions 82(a) & 82(b):
Let $s$ and $t$ be two vertices in an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ having distinct positive edge weights. Let $[X,Y]$ be a partition of $V$ such that $s\in X$ and $t\in Y$. Consider the edge $e$ having the minimum weight amongst all those edges that have one vertex in $X$ and one vertex in $Y$.
82(a). The edge e must definitely belong to:
questions.subject: 7. Algorithms
questions.optB: the minimum weighted spanning tree of G
questions.optC: the weighted shortest path from s to t
questions.optD: each path from s to t
questions.optE: the weighted longest path from s to t
questions.referenceAnswer: The unique lightest edge crossing any cut belongs to every MST by the cut property. It need not lie on a shortest or longest s-to-t path, nor on every path. The scan has a blank A and labels the MST text B; the standard four-option reference labels it A. Source B is retained.

questions.text:
Source question 82(b)
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 82(a) & 82(b):
Let $s$ and $t$ be two vertices in an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ having distinct positive edge weights. Let $[X,Y]$ be a partition of $V$ such that $s\in X$ and $t\in Y$. Consider the edge $e$ having the minimum weight amongst all those edges that have one vertex in $X$ and one vertex in $Y$.
82(b). Let the weight of an edge e denote the congestion on that edge. The congestion on a path is defined to be the maximum of the congestions on the edges of the path. We wish to find the path from s to t having minimum congestion. Which one of the following paths is always such a path of minimum congestion?
questions.subject: 7. Algorithms
questions.optA: a path from s to t in the minimum weight spanning tree
questions.optB: a weighted shortest path from s to t
questions.optC: an Euler walk from s to t
questions.optD: Hamiltonian path from s to t
questions.referenceAnswer: For an MST path, remove its maximum-weight edge to expose a cut. Any alternative path crosses that cut and cannot have a smaller maximum edge, or replacing the tree edge would reduce the tree weight. Thus the MST path is a minimum-bottleneck path.

Source question 83(a)
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 83(a) & 83(b):
Consider the following expression grammar. The semantic rules for expression calculation are stated next to each grammar production.
$\begin{array}{ll}E\to\mathrm{number} & E.\mathrm{val}=\mathrm{number.val} \\ \phantom{E}\mid E\text{ '+' }E & E^{(1)}.\mathrm{val}=E^{(2)}.\mathrm{val}+E^{(3)}.\mathrm{val} \\ \phantom{E}\mid E\text{ ' }\times\text{ ' }E & E^{(1)}.\mathrm{val}=E^{(2)}.\mathrm{val}\times E^{(3)}.\mathrm{val};\end{array}$
The above grammar and the semantic rules are fed to a yacc tool (which is an LALR(1) parser generator) for parsing and evaluating arithmetic expressions. Which one of the following is true about the action of yacc for the given grammar?
questions.optA: It detects recursion and eliminates recursion
questions.optB: It detects reduce-reduce conflict, and resolves
questions.optC: It detects shift-reduce conflict, and resolves the conflict in favor of a shift over a reduce action
questions.optD: It detects shift-reduce conflict, and resolves the conflict in favor of a reduce over a shift action
questions.subject: 10. Compiler Design
questions.referenceAnswer: The ambiguous grammar allows shifting another operator or reducing an existing expression. Without precedence declarations, yacc defaults to shifting in a shift/reduce conflict. It does not eliminate recursion.

Source question 83(b)
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 83(a) & 83(b):
Consider the following expression grammar. The semantic rules for expression calculation are stated next to each grammar production.
$\begin{array}{ll}E\to\mathrm{number} & E.\mathrm{val}=\mathrm{number.val} \\ \phantom{E}\mid E\text{ '+' }E & E^{(1)}.\mathrm{val}=E^{(2)}.\mathrm{val}+E^{(3)}.\mathrm{val} \\ \phantom{E}\mid E\text{ ' }\times\text{ ' }E & E^{(1)}.\mathrm{val}=E^{(2)}.\mathrm{val}\times E^{(3)}.\mathrm{val};\end{array}$
Assume the conflicts in Part (a) of this question are resolved and an LALR(1) parser is generated for parsing arithmetic expressions as per the given grammar. Consider an expression $3\times2+1$. What precedence and associativity properties does the generated parser realize?
questions.optA: Equal precedence and left associativity; expression is evaluated to 7
questions.optB: Equal precedence and right associativity; expression is evaluated to 9
questions.optC: Precedence of $\times$ is higher than that of $+$, and both operators are left associative; expression is evaluated to 7
questions.optD: Precedence of $+$ is higher than that of $\times$, and both operators are left associative; expression is evaluated to 9
questions.subject: 10. Compiler Design
questions.referenceAnswer: Default shifting delays reduction so the expression groups as 3*(2+1)=9. Neither operator has declared precedence, and conflicts favor the right-side continuation. This is the equal-precedence, right-associative behavior in B.

Source question 84(a)
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 84(a) & 84(b):
We are given 9 tasks $T_1,T_2,\ldots,T_9$. The execution of each task requires one unit of time. We can execute one task at a time. $T_i$ has a profit $P_i$ and a deadline $d_i$; profit $P_i$ is earned if the task is completed before the end of the $d_i$th unit of time.
$$\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr}
\text{Task}&T_1&T_2&T_3&T_4&T_5&T_6&T_7&T_8&T_9\\\hline
\text{Profit}&15&20&30&18&18&10&23&16&25\\
\text{Deadline}&7&2&5&3&4&5&2&7&3
\end{array}$$
Are all tasks completed in the schedule that gives maximum profit?
questions.subject: 7. Algorithms
questions.referenceAnswer: Schedule descending-profit jobs in their latest available slot no later than their deadline. An optimum is T2,T7,T9,T5,T3,T1,T8 with profit 147, leaving T4 and T6. Exchanging T5 for the equal-profit T4 would require four tasks (T2,T4,T7,T9) by time 3 and is infeasible. Exhaustive feasible-subset enumeration confirms the selected subset is unique.

Statement for Linked Answer Questions 85(a) & 85(b):
Consider the following floating point format:
[IMG_1]
Mantissa is a pure fraction in sign-magnitude form.
The decimal number $0.239\times2^{13}$ has the following hexadecimal representation without normalization and rounding off
questions.subject: 9. Digital Logic
questions.referenceAnswer: The sign is 0. Excess-64 exponent for 13 is 77 (binary 1001101), placing 4D in the high byte. Truncate 0.239*256=61.184 to 61=0x3D for the eight fractional mantissa bits. The unnormalized representation is 4D 3D.

questions.text:
Source question 85(b)
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 85(a) & 85(b):
Consider the following floating point format:
[IMG_1]
Mantissa is a pure fraction in sign-magnitude form.
The normalized representation for the above format is specified as follows. The mantissa has an implicit 1 preceding the binary (radix) point. Assume that only 0's are padded in while shifting a field. The normalized representation of the above number $(0.239\times2^{13})$ is
questions.subject: 9. Digital Logic
questions.referenceAnswer: Using the preceding truncated field, 0.00111101 times 2^13 becomes 1.11101000 times 2^10. The exponent changes to 10+64=74=0x4A, and after discarding the implicit leading 1 and padding zeros the stored mantissa is E8. Hence 4A E8. Directly requantizing the exact decimal after normalization would give a different last bit; the question's shift-and-zero-pad instruction selects D.
